title: Utilization mosaic: pools by priority (7d) — 2026-10-12 export
content:
Context: weekly export of the dashboard that breaks GPU utilization out by cluster and pool, then groups by priority class. Goal: surface skew between priority pools (critical/standard/batch/burst), identify emergent saturation, and recommend short actions for the 24–72h runway.

Date range: 2026-10-05 -> 2026-10-11 (7 full days)
Generated by: infra-metrics-job v2.8 (bigquery export -> sheet)
Query used (simplified):
  SELECT cluster, pool, priority, region, DATE(window) as day, avg_util_pct, p95_latency_ms, queued_slots, preemptions
  FROM infra.gpu_utilization_daily
  WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-10-05' AND '2026-10-11'
  GROUP BY cluster, pool, priority, region, day

Executive summary:
- Fleet-average utilization (7d weighted by GPU-hours): 64.1% (target operating band: 55-70%).
- Critical pools are at 79.4% avg (above preferred cap of 75%) with a rising 3-day trend.
- Standard pools: 62.0% avg with pronounced weekday peaks and nightly troughing.
- Batch/burst pools: 35.8% avg but high variance (range: 8% -> 87%) — several pools show underutilized pockets alongside microbursts.
- Top 3 congested clusters (by 95th p95 latency and queued slots): cl-us-west-3, cl-eu-central-2, cl-apac-sg-1. Total queued_slots across fleet peaking 2.3k on 2026-10-08.

Observations and anomalies:
- cl-apac-sg-1 burst-pool shows extreme volatility; on 2026-10-08 we saw a coordinated batch job causing a microburst that consumed ~87% of pool capacity for 2 hours and produced ~610 queued slots system-wide due to token-limited placement in that region. Investigate job origin (likely nightly data-augmentation).
- Preemption spikes concentrated in batch-io (us-east-1) — 12 preemptions over the week tied to a single job owner tag: team-data-pipeline. Ask solutions-eng to move that workload into isolated burst reservations or stagger windows.
- Critical pools (especially cl-us-west-3) have been creeping up; if trend continues, SLA headroom < 5% in 9 days at current growth rate. Consider short-term reservation bump or cross-region spill policy.

7-day per-cluster microtrend snapshots (one-line per cluster, day values are avg_util_pct):
cl-us-west-3: 72,74,76,78,80,82,83
cl-eu-central-2: 71,72,73,74,76,77,78
cl-apac-sg-1: 10,9,20,87,80,45,21
cl-us-east-1: 32,30,28,26,30,35,25
cl-eu-west-1: 48,45,44,60,58,52,39

Suggested short actions (0-72h):
- Immediate: throttle onboarding of new critical reservations in us-west until we add capacity or implement spill. Add a temporary policy to route non-critical traffic to eu-west or us-east when cl-us-west-3 critical pool >78%. (Owner: Marcus)
- Medium: schedule team-data-pipeline to use burst reservations or weekly stagger (Owner: Jing / Solutions Eng)
- Investigate: origin of the 2026-10-08 spike in apac sg burst pool and whether job can be rate-limited or replicated across apac eu (Owner: Noah)
- Longer: evaluate 50-GPU short-term reserve purchase for us-west for the next 30 days to relieve peak risk during holiday ramp. Finance/Procurement pre-approve option. (Owner: Aisha)

Notes to self / heuristics captured while exporting:
- We used GPU-hour weighting for fleet averages to avoid small pool noise.
- p95_latency_ms is derived from model-init + scheduling queue; confounded when preemptions are frequent.
- Some pools report artificially high queued_slots during brief AZ outages; cross-check with kube-machine events for pod churn.

Raw CSV attached in tab named "mosaic-7d-export" in the sheet.
Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/infra/gpu-utilization-mosaic?orgId=1&from=2026-10-05&to=2026-10-11
Follow-ups / tickets to create:
- INFRA-7401: Auto-route non-critical to secondary regions when critical pool >78% (priority: P2)
- INFRA-7402: Investigate preemption patterns on batch-io (us-east-1) and add runner tagging guardrails (priority: P3)
- INFRA-7403: Root-cause apac-sg-1 burst microburst (collect job metadata and pod logs) (priority: P1)
